patch.objective: Recommending a backup and recovery solution for databases

sources.cite: Microsoft Learn, Study guide for Exam AZ-305: Designing Microsoft Azure Infrastructure Solutions (page last updated 2026-10-30): Design identity, governance, and monitoring solutions 25-30%, Design data storage solutions 20-25%, Design business continuity solutions 15-20%, Design infrastructure solutions 30-35%
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Bullets quoted there: 'Recommend an application configuration management solution' (Design an application architecture); 'Recommend a monitoring solution'; 'Recommend a backup and recovery solution for compute'. The objective wording is the course seed's. (read for this round by an earlier pass on 2026-11-17)

sources.cite: Microsoft Learn, Restore a database from a backup in Azure SQL Database
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Relevant text: a point-in-time restore 'creates a new database on the same server as the original database'; 'You can't overwrite an existing database during restore'; recovery time depends on size, compute, log volume and activity to replay; to recover from user error either restore and swap names with ALTER DATABASE, or 'write and run a data recovery script that extracts the data from the restored database and applies it to the original'. That a swap loses every change made after the restore point follows from the page (it is not stated there). The az sql db restore flags (--dest-name, --time in ISO 8601) match the 'Restore a single database to an earlier point in time' CLI sample (read 2026-11-18).
